transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-23
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Leah (Redwood SE), Omar (Redwood CSM), Maya Carter (Atlas Eng Mgr), Diego Ramos (Atlas SRE), Priya Singh (Atlas Security), Ethan White (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, request logs and debugging flows. Customer primarily concerned with latency SLOs, error triage, and security/compliance (KMS/SOC2) for a planned pilot in Jan.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick intros \u0004 I'm Samir, i run the AE covering healthcare accounts. Leah our SE will walk through the console and the tracing flows.
00:12 Speaker 2 (Leah): hi team, thanks, i'll share my screen in a sec, the plan is: show live traces, error analysis, request logs, how to jump from trace to raw request payloads and then demo a debugging flow with a model fallback we use for latency spikes.
00:27 Speaker 3 (Maya): sounds good, quick context \u0004 we run a multi-tenant inference pipeline, about 2k rps at peak, mostly chat completions and some reranking. compliance and data residency are big for us.
00:40 Speaker 1 (Samir): great, and Diego on the SRE side?
00:44 Speaker 4 (Diego): yep, i'm Diego. main pain is intermittent 500s and tail latency spikes when sequences hit 6k tokens, and we need better visibility than our current logging.
00:56 Speaker 5 (Priya): priya here, security \u0004 we need KMS integration, SSO/SAML, audit logs, and proof of encryption at rest.
01:06 Speaker 2 (Leah): thanks, that's exactly what the console flows target. sharing screen now \u0004 looks like i got the tracing dashboard up. (screen share noise)
01:25 Speaker 2 (Leah): so this is the Traces tab, each trace groups a single user request across the serving runtime: routing, model step, kv cache lookup, token generation. note the trace waterfall \u0004 you can expand each span to see kernel selection, compilation times etc.
01:45 Speaker 2 (Leah): small note \u0004 sometimes the auto-transcript writes 'red wood' here, that's our internal bug with voice to text, ignore.
01:55 Speaker 2 (Leah): here's a sample failed request, you can see a 502 returned by the model shard, the span shows a kernel OOM on an optimized op, and we automatically routed to a fallback variant.
02:15 Speaker 1 (Samir): can you show the correlation to request logs?
02:19 Speaker 2 (Leah): yea click the right panel "Request Log" and it shows the raw request payload (truncated), headers, tokens used, and route decisions. you can also download the full request for debugging.
02:35 Speaker 4 (Diego): is the request payload sanitized? we can't send PII off-prem.
02:40 Speaker 2 (Leah): good question \u0004 by default hosted keeps request logs for 30 days, but for Private/Dedicated we can disable payload retention and keep only metadata and hashes. for your POC we can configure no payload retention and KMS-wrap the metadata.
02:58 Speaker 5 (Priya): what about encryption keys \u0004 HSM or customer-managed KMS?
03:03 Speaker 2 (Leah): we support customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) in Private deployments; for Hosted we offer CMEK with limited rotation controls.
03:15 Speaker 1 (Samir): also we'll attach the SOC2 PDF after the call.
03:20 Speaker 6 (Ethan): how does the tracing overhead look \u0004 will adding tracing add latency?
03:25 Speaker 2 (Leah): traces are sampled by default (1-5% for high traffic models) and span collection is async; the instrumentation adds sub-ms overhead in most cases. you can adjust sampling per route in the console.
03:45 Speaker 2 (Leah): switching to Error Analysis view \u0004 this aggregates errors by signature across models/routes. here's a cluster of 'invalid tokenization' errors that looks like a tokenizer boundary condition for the 4k->8k context switch.
04:05 Speaker 4 (Diego): can we get alerts on regressions? say a spike in bad generations or hallucinations?
04:12 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes, Redwood Optimize integrates with the console to run quality monitors against prompt sets and can trigger regression alerts. you can also wire alerts into PagerDuty or Slack from the console.
04:28 Speaker 3 (Maya): what's the fidelity of the request logs for debugging model-decision logic? can we see model inputs and tool calls?
04:34 Speaker 2 (Leah): you can capture full inputs and function/tool call traces for POC environments; for production we recommend capturing hashes plus sampled payloads to balance cost and privacy. also the trace links directly to the KV cache hit/miss span.
04:52 Speaker 2 (Leah): here's a request that slowed down because the K V cache missed and we had to regen a long prefix \u0004 notice the long stall at the cache lookup span.
05:05 Speaker 4 (Diego): that matches what we see during traffic bursts. can you show how to reproduce and test locally?
05:12 Speaker 2 (Leah): for debugging you can replay a request from the request log into a sandbox model variant; there's a "Replay" button that will run the request against pinned model + quantization profile and return traces.
05:28 Speaker 1 (Samir): that replay feature is handy \u0004 do you have rate limits or cost for replays?
05:33 Speaker 2 (Leah): replays are logged and billable at lower test rates, and for Dedicated customers we give a staging quota. we'll include replay pricing in the sheet.
05:50 Speaker 2 (Leah): jumping to the debugging flow \u0004 i'll simulate a model fallback. (types) here's a request that hit a kernel OOM, the serving runtime retried on a compatible quantized variant. you can see the fallback span and the percent increase in latency and token cost.
06:10 Speaker 3 (Maya): in that fallback can you force route back to the primary once it's healthy?
06:14 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes, rollouts and fallback policies are config-driven; we support auto-heal and canary rollouts, with manual override.
06:25 Speaker 4 (Diego): curious about observability \u0004 can we export traces to our in-house APM?
06:30 Speaker 2 (Leah): you can export traces and request logs via streaming connectors to OpenTelemetry collectors, or push to S3/MinIO for long-term retention. we have a prebuilt Datadog and Lightstep integration.
06:45 Speaker 5 (Priya): do exported logs maintain encryption in transit?
06:48 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit, and you can configure SSE+KMS for S3 exports.
07:00 Speaker 2 (Leah): now i'll show how to pivot from an error cluster to affected users and trace timelines. clicking the error cluster shows the top root causes, with filters for model version, region, and route.
07:28 Speaker 2 (Leah): notice this spike around 11:02 \u0004 drilling into timeline we see increased compilation time for a new kernel. that was when the runtime switched to a new CUDA kernel set.
07:48 Speaker 6 (Ethan): is there a playbook for kernel-related regressions? we run a strict SLA with partners.
07:54 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes, we keep a compatibility matrix by GPU type and model architecture; if a kernel causes regressions we auto-fallback and mark the build as suspect. we can also open a support ticket with priority.
08:08 Speaker 3 (Maya): about PII \u0004 i keep hearing 'download full request' \u0004 is that only for Private?
08:15 Speaker 2 (Leah): hosted can be configured to scrub payloads; full payload downloads are typically only available for Dedicated/Private, or Hosted with explicit retention opt-in and DPA clauses.
08:30 Speaker 4 (Diego): what's the retention window and can we meet EU data residency?
08:34 Speaker 2 (Leah): retention windows are configurable per account; for EU residency we deploy Private control planes in EU regions and can ensure logs stay in-region.
08:48 Speaker 2 (Leah): switching to Request Logs \u0004 you can query by trace id, request id, model, route, user id, and time range. queries are fast for last 30 days, and we have archive for longer.
09:05 Speaker 2 (Leah): the request log row includes tokens generated, prompt size, KV cache hit rate, model variant, runtime node id, and a link to the full trace.
09:18 Speaker 4 (Diego): do you capture per-token timings? we need that for micro-optimizations.
09:22 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes, per-token timing is available in the trace span details (tokenization micro-spans) \u0004 note it increases payload size, so it's sampled.
09:36 Speaker 3 (Maya): can we get a feed of errors into our ticketing system?
09:40 Speaker 2 (Leah): absolutely \u0004 webhook connector to Jira/ServiceNow with structured payloads (error id, trace link, affected routes).
09:50 Speaker 1 (Samir): one sec \u0004 Leah, can you demo a real incident from a recent customer (anonymized)?
09:58 Speaker 2 (Leah): sure, i'll open a past incident \u0004 here's one where a model version rollout caused 5xx spikes; the error analysis shows the culprit commit and the runtime auto-failed over to the previous version, then the team rolled forward with a patched kernel.
10:20 Speaker 6 (Ethan): are rollback windows automatic? how do you ensure no data loss?
10:25 Speaker 2 (Leah): rollbacks are quick; we keep pinned model versions and can divert new traffic while in-flight requests drain. request logs remain intact for post-mortem if retention is enabled.
10:40 Speaker 4 (Diego): does your console surface which customers were affected in multi-tenant Dedicated setups?
10:46 Speaker 2 (Leah): for Dedicated it's per-tenant, for Hosted we surface tenant ids if you pass them in request metadata; for Private it's fully scoped to the account.
10:58 Speaker 5 (Priya): any certification gaps we should know?
11:01 Speaker 1 (Samir): we are SOC2 certified and pursuing ISO 27001; i'll attach the latest report.
11:10 Speaker 5 (Priya): good, we'll need SAML SSO mapping to Okta and role-based access control.
11:16 Speaker 2 (Leah): RBAC is supported: roles, route-level permissions, and audit logs. we can demo SSO in the POC.
11:28 Speaker 3 (Maya): one more \u0004 can we retroactively scrub a captured payload if a user requests deletion?
11:34 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes with Private/Dedicated you can run a data erasure job; for Hosted we have a subject access request process and can purge retained payloads per the DPA.
11:48 Speaker 2 (Leah): demoing query builder now \u0004 i'll filter for errors in route "patient-summarize" during the time window last Wednesday.
12:01 Speaker 2 (Leah): see this list, click an entry and open the trace \u0004 trace shows a long token generation span because of a fallback to a non-quantized model.
12:18 Speaker 4 (Diego): how do you determine when to quantize vs not?
12:22 Speaker 2 (Leah): Redwood Optimize recommends quantization profiles based on throughput targets and quality evals; you can test profiles via replay before applying.
12:36 Speaker 6 (Ethan): what's the expected CPU/GPU savings using the recommended profiles?
12:40 Speaker 2 (Leah): typically 30-60% token cost reduction depending on model and workload; we'll include model-by-model estimates in the spreadsheet.
12:58 Speaker 1 (Samir): quick commercial note \u0004 Dedicated gets you predictable capacity and privacy controls; Hosted is faster to start. we'll map options after you confirm POC size.
13:16 Speaker 3 (Maya): for the POC we'll want Dedicated in a short-term staging pool if possible, otherwise Private control plane.
13:24 Speaker 1 (Samir): understood \u0004 we'll propose both options. Leah, any closing demo bits?
13:30 Speaker 2 (Leah): final flow: we showed trace -> request log -> replay -> debug -> apply rollback/rollout. i'll also show automated regression alerts: set a baseline prompt set, we compute quality metrics and alert on drift.
13:48 Speaker 5 (Priya): will drift alerts include sample failing prompts?
13:51 Speaker 2 (Leah): yes, and you can attach them to an eval and push to a model comparison report.
14:04 Speaker 6 (Ethan): timing on POC start? we were thinking early Jan.
14:08 Speaker 1 (Samir): we can kickoff week of Jan 5th; i'll follow up with a calendar invite once we align stakeholders.
14:18 Speaker 3 (Maya): ok thanks, gonna circulate internally.
14:23 Speaker 2 (Leah): one more note \u0004 trace sampling, payload retention, and replay quotas are all per-account settings; we'll template recommended settings for healthcare.
14:36 Speaker 4 (Diego): any last technical cautions about kernel incompatibilities?
14:40 Speaker 2 (Leah): keep models pinned during canaries, monitor compilation spans; we can set auto-fallback to quantized variants to reduce OOM risk.
14:52 Speaker 1 (Samir): great \u0004 recap of next steps: i'll send SOC2 and pricing; Leah will share benchmark and trace exports; Maya will confirm POC stakeholders and timeline.
15:05 Speaker 3 (Maya): thanks all, looking forward.
15:10 Speaker 1 (Samir): thanks everyone, we'll follow up. bye.

Notes: transcript has typical Fireflies artifacts \u0004 occasional mislabels, minor transcription errors (K V vs KV, red wood). Links shared during call: SOC2 doc (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), POC onboarding template (link).
